children: Max Estates shares will remain in focus after the company said it will enter into a joint development agreement (JDA) for a ~9.76-acre land parcel in Indirapuram, Ghaziabad.
The project has a super built-up development potential of ~1.5 million sq ft and an estimated gross development value (GDV) of ₹2,500-3,000 crore.
The proposed transaction is subject to satisfactory completion of due diligence, receipt of all requisite approvals and execution of the JDA.
Catch all market action in our live blog

Last month, the company acquired approximately 84.71-acre West Delhi land parcel in a non-cash share-swap transaction. The deal offers an estimated gross development value (GDV) of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore over the next few years.
In the previous trading session, the share closed at Rs 601.80, up Rs 6.00, or 1.01 percent.

The share touched a 52-week high of Rs 623.95 and a 52-week low of Rs 305.55 on 21 September, 2026 and 30 March, 2026, respectively. Currently, the stock is trading 3.55 percent below its 52-week high and 96.96 percent above its 52-week low.
The market capitalisation of the company stands at Rs 9,844.24 crore.

title: Max Estates share price in focus on ₹3,000-cr Ghaziabad development deal
